title: Impact of Recent Price Increases on Cost of Living
what_it_is: Impact of Recent Price Increases on Cost of Living

sections.label: 2017 CPI inflation projection
sections.summary: MTI and MAS project CPI-All Items inflation to rise to 0.5% to 1.5% in 2017, driven mainly by higher electricity and energy prices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
sentences.text: For 2017, MTI and MAS have projected that the Consumer Price Index (CPI)-All Items inflation will pick up to 0.5% to 1.5%, from -0.5% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
sentences.text: The main driver of the pickup in inflation in 2017 is the expected increase in the prices of electricity and other energy-related components, such as petrol, on the back of a projected rise in global oil prices.

sections.label: Administrative price adjustments impact
sections.summary: Administrative price adjustments, including water tariff and car park charge increases, will add around 0.2 percentage point to 2017 inflation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
sentences.text: At the same time, administrative price adjustments, including the increases in water tariff and car park charges, will also contribute to a temporary increase in inflation, although I must say the impact is expected to be small.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
sentences.text: MTI estimates that the various administrative price adjustments will collectively contribute around 0.2 percentage point to inflation in 2017.

sections.label: Rebates excluded from CPI
sections.summary: The 0.2 percentage-point figure excludes rebates and subsidies; water tariffs rise in two tranches and U-Save rebates are not counted in CPI.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On the question about whether the 0.2 percentage-point increase includes some of the rebates and Government subsidies, the answer is no.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: One, of course, is to stagger the price increases, and as Members would remember, the water tariffs are increased over two tranches: the first tranche will be in July this year, and the next increment will be in July next year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The U-Save rebates are not taken into account in the CPI calculations, as these are actually given to households as a lump sum to be utilised over a few months.

sections.label: Rebates reduce household impact
sections.summary: U-Save rebates are not captured in CPI adjustments, so households receiving rebates will feel a much smaller impact than reported.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Therefore, when you look at the top-line adjustments for CPI, bear in mind that hidden behind it, there is also some form of U-Save rebates, for example, that are not captured in the adjustment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, for households that receive rebates, the impact for them will be much less than what is reported.
